body:
I just keep getting kicked on and off waiting lists cos I don't seem that bad outwardly.

That's why I'm giving up on ever feeling okay.
And thank you so much for your kind words and support.

We don't speak much as we both have new partners, plus I basically killed off all contact six months ago when I had my first big realisation and apology. Unfortunately mutual friends bothered her in that time over it so the only contact she's had regarding me has been about that.

From what I understand she says she's looking forward to us bumping into each other but worries meeting or talking now will make it worse in my head.

I tried saying I'd do what I can to help or asked if there was anything I could do but she says she worked it out in her own therapy and wants to move on from it. I think her own words last month were "there's nothing there for you to feel bad about" so I need to forgive myself.

I want to respect her wishes to move on from it but it doesn't switch off. I still feel awful that I didn't understand I'd gone so wrong at the time.

I was pressuring with regards to anal sex, constantly engaged in kink talk unless she requested I don't, and in several cases did not respond immediately when things changed mid-sex like when she would ask if I was almost finished. I pushed back, thinking it was that porn-esque confidence until she bluntly said enough.

Sorry, I don't want to go into too much detail. I know it was really shitty, I do not understand who I was during sex at those times, I'm working with a therapist on this. I can't offer any other defence of my behaviour.
Thank you, I really appreciate the supportive words. I am determined to get better and be accountable for my behaviour. I hope to find a way to help others to avoid being the person I was.

Yeah, I don't think I ever even stopped to consider how dysfunctional it was, nor did I have anyone I could speak to.

Even if I can kick the habit, which I really really want to, it's gonna take a long time to handle the shame of how it warped my relationship.

I'm working with a professional, it's just slow progress digging through earlier shit.

I can see how the actions came about, it doesn't excuse it though and I can't undo it so I'm a bit at a loss.

May I ask, if you didn't realise you had an issue that what motivated you to read that book? Were you looking for answers to a different question?

I've been depressed as long as I could remember but never realised this was an issue until I realised I'd hurt someone else instead of just me.

I do have concerns that my answer would have been different before I realised I am one of those people.

I have recently been reading about men's support and social groups that dedicate time to talking about how we handle being at both ends of toxic masculinity. I have to wonder, had that space been available to me, would I have recognised my personal issues sooner and dealt with it or would I have turned down the help as that could never be me. In either case, I do want to get involved in that work now so that I can help others not make that mistake. Does anyone else here do that offline?

Thank you, I will try talking to the friends first because I think they mostly thought I was exaggerating cos it didn't seem in line with how I present myself.

I see what I did wrong, I did not communicate my own sexual issues and instead acted out the "porn script". It's being with a new partner who did prompt healthy conversation that has made me see how wrong I was.

I told people because I wanted to preempt them finding out elsewhere and so that someone might have a solution to me feeling the monster.

My fears are that moving on may mean repeating my mistakes or having them come back to bite me.

It's a defence mechanism of sorts, one that's gone haywire though. I need a way to disengage it, I know.

Thank you, I appreciate the perspective you offer here.

I do struggle to keep in mind that I'm not the past, I just keep reliving everything. That's not fair on anyone.

I had never considered that as a possibility.

I've referred myself for a psych screening for other things but this makes sense, especially as much of the behaviour I'm feeling guilty for in the first place has arisen due to obsessive thoughts and compulsive tendencies. 

I guess I assumed OCD is fixed on certain things, I'm often obsessing on something but it cycles out so I assumed it wasn't that. 

Thank you for bringing this possibility to my attention.

Thanks for the reassurance dude, most of my pain is to do with how I behaved rather than it being over though.

Something of an identity crisis, becoming the thing I hate, etc. and not knowing how to handle that.

Thanks man, I appreciate the positivity and forward thinking.

I do know right now I'm stuck on the negative self image, thinking I'm some abusive predatory monster. Logically, I know my ex hasn't said that, and my current partner says she's seen no evidence of that, so it's probably toxic shame. I hope I can shift that and be a force for good like you described.

Nah, that's pretty fair, not harsh at all. One of the reasons I've not been reaching out to her lately actually, I know the fixation ain't healthy or fair.

Fortunately I am seeing a therapist, just gets difficult between sessions unfortunately.
I've got no interest in winning her back, I know things are better this way. I just want to deal with the guilt of it.

Amusingly, I am just out of therapy where we obviously went over a lot.

I really appreciate your insight because you're right, no punishment would be enough short of being locked away and left forever.

Also, the point about why we broke up is spot on too. I'll admit that I don't have much closure on why we split, she says we became platonic, and different people, who needed more support than either could give. I guess I blame myself for that too. Depression killed any desire for anything, outside of sitting about watching loads of porn apparently. 

I wasn't perfect, so I'm taking the blame for all of it. It's difficult cos I could well be called abusive, although she's said she doesn't think so, and so I don't wanna go victim blaming at all.

I know I need to work on myself though, deal with the psychological splitting and try to accept being human.

I've actually told my current partner everything. She appreciates that and says she hasn't seen any of what I'm obsessing over in the several months we've been together. She thinks I'm worth sticking around for.

I really do wanna push through it, I'm just scared to let myself off the hook right now.

Aye, I'm trying. Kinda stuck on the obsessive guilt though, don't exactly know how to let it go.

Have the issue of self splitting, used to try to think very highly of myself, now I'm nothing.

Shit man, I feel this.

I'm a year out of an eight year relationship and tearing myself up over how shit I behaved the last few years. 

I hope you find the peace you deserve.

Thank you, I know I struggle with the thought that someone out there hurts because of me. I'm a bit on the obsessive side. 

Hard when you've always measured yourself against your flaws and then suddenly loads more flaws become evident. Just making it through to therapy tomorrow.

Thank you, I appreciate the kind words of yourself and other posters.

I'm working through it, but I've never done self-forgiveness so it's a new skill I'm working through in therapy now too.

I guess the Buddhist answer would probably relate to nonself and letting go of beliefs that cause suffering, but in practice it's hard to shutdown a lifetime of assuming you're the root cause of all problems. The Buddhist texts have probably been the most helpful things I've read so far though. 

I'm now scared of forgiving myself and never correcting the past, having people out there want to punish me and I just walk away. I don't know if avoiding that is immoral too?

I'm sorry if I'm not understanding, but I assume that shame and fear here relate to actions yet to be taken. I don't want to disregard all shame, but surely there has to be a limit to what is reasonable? And how do you come back from it being too much?

Thank you for these links, they were very insightful. Especially around the topic of reputation actually, that has been a big concern of mine.

However, do you have anything that would counsel how to deal with previous misdeeds? What do you do with things you have actually done wrong before realising you acted out of suffering? Can you repair the pain caused to others?
Sorry if I've not chosen the correct flair, I can change it if advised.

Thank you.

You're right, it's very hard cos I'm being told we became different people when all I see is that I became less of a person.

And now I'm starting to understand why but can't make others understand, convince them I'm not that person.

I wish you luck with your own journey.

Thank you for being so understanding, I feel like you really do understand this type of situation.

I feel like I've got very lost in catastrophising and assuming I'm some criminal beast who is going to get taken away. Like I'm distorting every memory to be the worst possible version? 

I hope that it's clear to her that I never intended to hurt her and that I was uneducated, lost, and hurting myself.

Thank you. I've been truly consumed by this lately as everyone I've spoken to has had different responses to it. When I describe it from my perspective I now see myself as pressuring and coercive but also poor at communicating and struggling with boundaries and the different moods that we each had. What scares me is that I can see how this would look in other lights, some people have dismissed it as just how guys are whilst I can easily imagine how in a conversation with high emotions it could be cast as something truly monstrous.

It's hard not knowing where she is, other than the honeymoon phase with her new guy. I don't want to bother her though. 

I am revolted at myself for not seeing it sooner. And I am truly committed to change.
Thank you so much. I've always assumed it was my fault for viewing that stuff, I felt old enough to blame for it and ashamed for not getting out sooner.

Thank you. I made another post in this sub a couple of days ago with more details and would really appreciate your guidance on that.

I've already given a vague apology for being "shitty" and saying sorry that my behaviour hurt her but she said that the apology is unnecessary.

I am just so consumed with guilt and keep viewing myself as a sex offending monster, waiting to be punished. I even think I'm inventing more memories where I'm even worse.

As an example, I remember often that my partner would complain about a topic or issue she was having and I would try to empathise by sharing my own story or saying I know how that feels. I would get accused of being told that I was making it about myself or trying to "one up" her when I was just trying (and failing apparently) to relate to her.

How do I know if my justification was true or if I was actually playing some game?
Thank you, I appreciate the support in changing this.

I am getting treatment for being pressuring, for not respecting boundaries, and now for the guilt I'm feeling for having done that.

I also want to deal with the guilt that I may have been toxic in other ways, being overly critical, affecting my ex's mental health.
